I saved the Q3 results to `/work/answer.json`. Running the same script on Q2 reproduced all 10 of your reference values exactly.

| Question | Q3 value |
|---|---|
| a. Top segment and net sales | smb, 316,534,383 |
| b. Customers with paid orders | 248 |
| c. Top category and net sales | svc, 312,755,660 |
| d. Month with the highest net sales | 2025-07 |
| e. Customer with the largest refund total | u93@ex.com |
| f. Customers with 2+ paid orders | 240 |
| g. Average net sales per order | 692,548 |
| h. Growth from August to September | -3.3% |

To match the Q2 reference values, I had to settle three things the definitions left open:
- **Time zone:** The order times in the DB are in UTC. Splitting quarters and months by those UTC dates did not match the Q2 values, so I converted the times to Korean time (UTC+9) first.
- **Segment spelling:** The same segment is written different ways (e.g. `SMB`, ` consumer`, `Enterprise `). I stripped spaces and lowercased them before grouping.
- **Duplicate customers:** There are 300 customer records but only 250 distinct emails. For b, e and f, I treated customers sharing an email as one customer. Without this, b and f did not match the Q2 values.

STATUS: DONE
